description: The words Portal's people use, held to the model-written layer: construct records and flows may not use an `avoid` word or miscase a proper noun, and every term must be used by at least one of them. Definitions follow docs/GLOSSARY.md and README.md; each term cites a line that uses it.

terms.definition: The native macOS and iOS app for one person running a team of AI agents on hardware they own; this repository.
The agent platform Portal talks to. The Hermes gateway Portal requires is the `ethenotethan/harness` fork of `NousResearch/hermes-agent`.
An upstream or default Hermes install managed over plain HTTP; it can be administered from Portal but cannot create or stream Portal chat sessions.

distinguish_from.Hermes: Hermes is the platform and its gateway; Hermes Standard is a stock install reached over HTTP that cannot serve chat.

terms.definition: A second agent platform, spoken to over REST and SSE, that can sit behind the same chat UI as the Hermes gateway.
The system credential store where Portal keeps gateway secrets out of plain files.
The connection the Hermes gateway is reached over; Portal shares one per gateway.
The request, response and event protocol Portal speaks to the Hermes gateway over its WebSocket.
Apple's beta distribution service, where signed iOS builds of Portal are uploaded after a merge or tag.
Apple's desktop operating system; one of the two platforms Portal ships on.
Apple's phone operating system; one of the two platforms Portal ships on.
Apple's declarative UI framework; every Portal view is a SwiftUI view.
The Swift linter whose custom rules carry Portal's architectural checks, run under `--strict` against a frozen baseline.
Where the repository lives and where its workflows run as GitHub Actions.
The system preferences store Portal uses for small non-secret settings.
The Hermes backend specifically: a WebSocket JSON-RPC server Portal connects to, one per person.

distinguish_from.backend: A backend is any agent platform behind the chat UI; the gateway is the Hermes one.

terms.definition: The agent platform behind the chat UI: the Hermes gateway, or Centaur over REST and SSE.

distinguish_from.gateway: The gateway is the Hermes backend; say backend only when the statement holds for every platform.

terms.definition: One Hermes agent session: a conversation with its own history, model and skills, listed by the gateway.
One user prompt plus the assistant's full response to it.

distinguish_from.session: A turn is one exchange inside a session.

terms.definition: A typed event the gateway emits on the stream; the event type of the whole chat pipeline.
A named, persistent artifact the agent maintains across turns and sessions: any fenced block carrying an `id` upserts into the store.
The live graph of tool invocations in one conversation turn, drawn as lanes over time.
The tree of a root prompt and the subagents it delegated to, recursively.
An agent another agent delegated work to; a child in the spawn tree.
A named capability the gateway can enable per session.
A scheduled job the gateway runs, listed and managed through `cron.manage`.
The knowledge base of pages and links the agents maintain and Portal browses.
One recorded edit to the wiki.
Where tool approvals, clarifications and notifications wait for the person running Portal.
A structured course of ordered modules whose steps are written lessons or quizzes, with per-step progress.
